outcome: Say when an export's date or timestamp pattern rendered nothing: a per-column pattern on a column whose values are not dates or timestamps, or a file-level pattern in a file with no such value, is named in the export response instead of being reported as rendered
criteria: A successful export whose format_spec gives a column a date_format or timestamp_format that no value of that column took (its values are text or numbers), or gives a file-level pattern that no value in the file took, reports each such column in the response: its logical type, how many of its values there are, and how many of them read as ISO dates or timestamps
The summary no longer says the values were rendered with the specification when a pattern rendered nothing; it names the columns the pattern did not apply to

The response carries format_not_applied advice explaining that a pattern formats date and timestamp columns only and, when the values read as dates, that a derive with try_cast(column as date) before the export makes the pattern apply

Tests on data unrelated to any benchmark cover a per-column pattern on a text column of ISO dates, one on prose dates, a file-level pattern with no temporal column, a pattern that did apply (no report), and a mixed file; the test suite passes; README's export section says what the response reports

reason: Counting which values read as ISO dates or timestamps uses the patterns MADR 0006 documents for import-time temporal refinement, so the count agrees with what import would have typed as temporal; that decision constrains the work and was not bound at the seal

dispositions.note: tests/test_export.py covers the five cases on shipment and talk data; the full suite passes except 8 FFmpeg tests in tests/test_audio.py and tests/test_perception.py whose fixtures encode video with libx264, which this host's FFmpeg build lacks; the same 8 fail on the unchanged tree

note: ValueRenderer counts, per column, the non-null values it rendered and how many were dates or timestamps, and reports the columns a pattern formatted nothing of: a column's own pattern whenever its values held no date or timestamp, a file-level pattern only when it formatted nothing anywhere in the file, and then on every covered column with values (numbers included). export_result counts ISO date and timestamp values of those columns with a new engine scan (count_iso_temporal, the MADR 0006 import test), returns format_not_applied, records it in the dataset.exported audit event, replaces the rendered sentence in the summary, and attaches format_not_applied advice. The advice names try_cast(column as date|timestamp) when values read as dates, and rewrites the request as materialize_result (derive, select in order, rename) plus the same export when every such column casts without losing a value. README and the export_result tool description say what is reported.
